summary: The school district urges the FCC to preserve and strengthen the E-Rate program, rejecting proposals to sunset or eliminate it, and emphasizes the ongoing need for reliable broadband infrastructure for modern public education.

claims.argument: Reducing E-Rate would increase costs for districts like East Hampton Public Schools
claims.evidence_quote: East Hampton Public Schools has received $283,375 in committed federal E-Rate support over funding years 2021–2025 — an average of roughly $56,675 a year toward the connections our students depend on. That support does not represent a one-time build; it is the recurring cost of keeping a modern network running.
